newsitem.title: USA: General Dynamics says net earnings fall.
newsitem.headline: General Dynamics says net earnings fall.

text.p: Defence contractor General Dynamics said Wednesday its earnings rose about 9 percent in the third quarter, excluding discontinued operations, and cited cost reductions for some of the gain.
The Fall Church. Va.-based company reported earnings from continuing operations of $68 million, or $1.08 per share, vs. $62 million, or 99 cents per share, a year ago.
The company's net earnings, however, fell to $68 million, compared with $91 million in the third quarter of 1995, which included $29 million associated with discontinued operations.
Third-quarter 1996 sales were $862 million, compared with $718 million in the same period last year.
"We've continued to reduce costs programme by programme -- improving prices for our customers and profit margins for our shareholders," General Dynamics Chairman James Mellor said.
"All of our programmes are strong and healthy, we're generating free cash flow of more than $200 million per year, and our backlog of business is growing."
Mellor said the defence appropriations bill recently signed by President Clinton included funding for all the company's programmes, including the third and final Seawolf submarine.

"Design work for the follow-on to Seawolf, the New Attack Submarine, is proceeding under a $1.3 billion design contract signed earlier in the year. This will be a 30-ship programme, and production will begin in 1998," Mellor said.
General Dynamics stock was down $1.125 at $68.625 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
